readme:
# Build Your Own Interpreter

Implement an interpreter for a Lox-like language in Rust, based on Crafting Interpreters.

## Stages

1. Lexer/Tokenizer: Scan source code into tokens (keywords, identifiers, literals, operators)
2. Parser/AST: Parse tokens into an Abstract Syntax Tree using recursive descent
3. Evaluator: Walk the AST and evaluate expressions to produce values
4. Variables and Scope: Add variable declarations (var), assignments, and block scoping
5. Functions and Closures: Implement user-defined functions with closures

## Getting Started

Each stage builds on the previous one. Start with stage 1.

Run `cargo test` after implementing each stage.

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Expr {
    Number(f64),
    Str(String),
    Bool(bool),
    Nil,
    Ident(String),
    Binary { op: BinOp, left: Box<Expr>, right: Box<Expr> },
    Unary { op: UnaryOp, expr: Box<Expr> },
    Call { callee: Box<Expr>, args: Vec<Expr> },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum BinOp {
    Add, Sub, Mul, Div,
    Eq, Neq, Lt, Lte, Gt, Gte,
    And, Or,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum UnaryOp {
    Neg, Not,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Stmt {
    Expr(Expr),
    Print(Expr),
    Var { name: String, init: Expr },
    Block(Vec<Stmt>),
    If { condition: Expr, then_branch: Box<Stmt>, else_branch: Option<Box<Stmt>> },
    While { condition: Expr, body: Box<Stmt> },
    Func { name: String, params: Vec<String>, body: Box<Stmt> },
    Return(Expr),
}
